title: 2026-07-23 Tidehaven Health security & hosting evaluation
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2026-07-23 14:30 PT | Duration: ~46m | Recording: enabled
Attendees: Maya (Redwood AE), Daniel (Redwood SE), Sofia (Redwood SE) -- Laura (CTO), Marcus (SRE), Priya (Security)

Auto-gen summary (may be imperfect):
We walked through Tidehaven's security constraints for inference hosting. Primary drivers: PHI handling, EU data residency for some datasets, Okta SSO + SCIM provisioning, customer-managed KMS/HSM, SOC2/ISO evidence. Customer leaning toward Dedicated or Private because of compliance but wants clear cost/latency tradeoffs and an SLO for audit logs forwarding. Next steps: share SOC2 artifacts, SAML guide, architecture diagram and a Dedicated pilot quote.

[00:00] Maya: hi everyone, thanks for carving out time. quick intros, we'll do a short discovery on your security and hosting constraints, then daniel can answer infra questions. who wants to start with a one-liner on primary constraint?
[00:22] Laura: yeah sure, hi, im laura chen, cto at tidehaven. main thing for us is we handle sensitive patient intake notes; so PHI, so data residency and encryption are huge. we also need proof points we can show internal compliance e.g., SOC2.
[00:40] Priya: and from security side we need SSO via okta, scim for provisioning, rbac with least privilege, and the ability to export audit logs to our splunk. retention windows kind of matter too.
[01:05] Daniel: got it, thanks. quick q - do you have an existing requirement for SOC2 Type II or ISO27001 today? or is that on the roadmap?
[01:20] Priya: we have SOC2 Type II in progress; must be complete before production rollouts but for pilots we can use attestation docs. ISO is nice-to-have but not blocker.
[01:36] Marcus: we also need to ensure we can use our own kms / hsm for key management, ideally customer-managed keys in a VPC/private deployment.
[01:48] Sofia: good, that's helpful. two follow-ups: do you expect to run inference in EU for residency requirements, and any hard latency p95 targets?
[02:15] Laura: yes, a subset of eu data must stay regionally processed. latency target is under 200ms p95 for the chat assist flows; some batch embedding workloads are ok with higher latency.

[05:10] Daniel: brief overview - redwood supports hosted api, dedicated reserved pools, and private vpc/on-prem. For the dedicated/private options you can bring your own kms (we support cloud kms and customer-managed hsm integrations). Audit logs can stream to syslog/s3 and we have export hooks for splunk. note: some of the product names in our notes may be transcribed oddly - we call it Redwood Dedicated (sometimes the transcript says "redwood dedike"), the runtime uses prefix caching, kv cache (sometimes transcribed as "kv cash").

[08:00] Priya: ok on audit logs - we need immutable logs with at least 90 day retention and real-time forwarding to splunk. can you guarantee immutability or do we need to layer a third-party?
[08:25] Daniel: logs are append-only on the control plane and we support exporting to external SIEM in near-real time. for immutability we recommend exporting to an S3 bucket with object lock and lifecycle policies on your side; we can help automate the export.

[11:30] Marcus: about encryption - do you encrypt at rest and in transit by default? and can we bring our key to the instance?
[11:45] Maya: yes, both in transit and at rest. for dedicated/private you can configure customer-managed KMS keys; we also support HSM-backed keys in some on-prem patterns.

[15:00] Laura: data residency: we'd like EU-only processing for the EU cohort, can you pin a model to an EU region and ensure no cross-region backup?
[15:28] Daniel: yes, we can pin model variants and routing policies to region; backups and snapshots can be controlled per deployment template. we discussed retention - we can set retention policies at the tenant level. sometimes our engineering notes mis-say "snapshot" as "snip-shot" in transcripts.

[18:40] Priya: SSO: Okta is our IdP; we need SAML SSO + SCIM for provisioning and RBAC sync. also require support for role separation - devs vs operators vs compliance.
[19:05] Sofia: we support SAML/SSO, SAML assertions, and SCIM for user provisioning; RBAC is configurable with role mapping and audit trails for role changes. we can demo the scim flow in a sandbox.

[22:05] Marcus: another constraint: auditability for model changes and rollouts - we need model versioning logs, who triggered a rollout, diffs.
[22:30] Daniel: we have per-route/model dashboards and trace hooks; rollouts are logged with user id, timestamp, and can be exported. it's in the console and also streamable to your audit system.

[25:20] Laura: what about cost concerns - dedicated looks appealing, but our finance is sensitive. what's the fallback? hosted for burst and dedicated for steady state? how does automatic fallback work?
[25:50] Maya: typical pattern is dedicated reserved capacity for steady workloads and hosted as fallback for spikes; routing policies can be configured by cost, latency, and region. we'll provide cost models in the quote.

[29:10] Priya: any third-party certifications e.g., pen tests, encryption attestations?
[29:25] Maya: we can share pen test summaries and a SOC2 prep pack; Redwood (host) maintains SOC2 for our hosted control plane; if you choose private we provide a package to help produce evidence for your auditors.

[33:00] Marcus: technical nit - do you allow us to bring docker images or do you require your runtime? some teams want a certifiable runtime for air-gapped on-prem installs.
[33:20] Daniel: for air-gapped we provide an on-prem package; it runs our runtime but we provide install docs and a checklist for hardening. you cannot swap the runtime binary but you can run it in your environment and integrate your KMS/HSM.

[36:25] Priya: retention policy question: logs retention minimum 90 days, but what about payload data? we need to define retention and deletion guarantees for request/response text.
[36:45] Sofia: request/response logs can be configured; hosted default is 30 days but we offer configurable retention for dedicated/private and can delete logs on a schedule. we document deletion flows and event logs for deletions for auditors.

[40:00] Laura: ok, success criteria for pilot: 1) SOC2 attestation shared, 2) Okta SSO + SCIM handshake in test, 3) KMS integration validated, 4) latency within 200ms p95 for chat sample, 5) audit logs streaming to splunk and retained 90 days. can we plan a 4-week pilot?
[40:32] Maya: yes, that sounds doable as a pilot scope. timeline - if we start next week we can have a sandbox and initial tests in 2-3 weeks.

[44:20] Maya: quick recap and next steps, we'll send the SOC2 pack, sso/saml scim guide, architecture diagram and a preliminary dedicated pilot quote. any other blockers?
[44:38] Priya: just internal legal review; we'll loop them in.
[44:50] Laura: thanks all, that was helpful.

Transcript notes: rough transcription quality medium - some product terms mangled, occasional speaker attribution errors. Some filler words removed for readability.
summary: Discovery with Tidehaven Health focused on security and hosting constraints for PHI workloads. Key points: SOC2 Type II in progress, Okta SSO + SCIM required, customer-managed KMS/HSM requested, EU data residency for subset of data, audit logs to Splunk with 90d retention, RBAC and model rollout auditability. Pilot scope proposed with technical validation (SSO, KMS, logs, latency), Redwood to provide SOC2 artifacts, SAML/SCIM guide, architecture diagram, and dedicated pilot quote.
